newsitem.title: NORWAY: Arafat back in Norway, denies stalling Mideast pact.
newsitem.headline: Arafat back in Norway, denies stalling Mideast pact.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrived in Norway on Monday, dismissing Israeli accusations he was stalling after negotiators failed to agree on a partial Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.

Arafat told reporters he had come to Norway to get "another push from outside" for peace as U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said he was leaving Israel, having failed in another all-night effort to wrap up a deal.
Ross said Arafat's European trip -- at the invitation of the Norwegian government, which played a key role in a 1993 pact on Palestinian self-rule -- would hamper mediation efforts.
But Arafat rejected this, saying: "It is going on. The subcommittees are going on."
The United States and Israel have been cool to a European role in the U.S.-brokered talks.
Arafat, who was given a red-carpet welcome at Oslo airport by Norwegian Foreign Minister Bjoern Tore Godal, said the trip had been planned since June.
"We are trying to do our best," he said. "Last night we did not sleep. I slept only in the airplane."
U.S. President Bill Clinton on Sunday urged both Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in separate telephone calls to seal a deal.

Palestinians have said their remaining differences centre on Israel's demand for a right to pursue Palestinian militants into parts of Hebron it hands over to the PLO and on what arms Palestinian police would be allowed to carry.

Netanyahu has insisted on modifying security arrangements set in a redeployment deal which Israel's previous Labour-led government signed with the PLO. About 400 Jewish settlers live in enclaves in Hebron among 100,000 Palestinians.
The troop redeployment has been delayed since March.
Palestinians have said Israel is trying to renegotiate terms of the Hebron withdrawal which the Jewish state agreed to more than a year ago.

Arafat, in Norway for two days on his first official visit since becoming president in January, shared the 1994 Nobel Peace Prize with then-Israeli foreign minister Shimon Peres and late prime minister Yitzhak Rabin for the now-troubled agreement on Palestinian self-rule.

On Tuesday, he was due to be received by King Harald V before holding final talks with Godal and leaving for Dublin, where the Palestinian leader will meet Ireland's prime minister, foreign minister and president during a two-day visit.
Ireland now holds the European Union presidency and Foreign Minister Dick Spring went to Israel and Gaza earlier this month to lend EU support to the peace process.
